```{python}
import seaborn as sns
from IPython.display import Markdown, display

# Locate the repository root, so this report may live at any depth under it.

             if (p / "pixi.toml").exists())
sys.path.insert(0, str(_root / "src"))
from arkhinfra import v3_common as c  # noqa: E402
from arkhinfra import v4_common as v4  # noqa: E402
from arkhinfra import egais as e  # noqa: E402
from arkhinfra import match_2022 as m  # noqa: E402

mpl.rcParams.update({
    "font.family": "DejaVu Sans",   # full Cyrillic coverage for figure labels
    "figure.dpi": 150,
    "axes.spines.top": False,
    "axes.spines.right": False,
    "axes.grid": True,
    "grid.alpha": 0.25,
    "axes.titlesize": 12,
    "axes.titleweight": "bold",
})

ACCENT, RISK, GREEN, PURPLE = c.ACCENT, c.RISK, c.GREEN, c.PURPLE
MIXED, OLD = c.MIXED, c.OLD
INK = "#1f2933"

# One colour per delivery, held fixed across every before/after chart so the
# reader never has to re-learn the legend.
SRC_COLORS = {"2022 study": PURPLE, "v3 export": OLD,
              "v4 layer": RISK, "Licence registry": GREEN}
# Evidence tier keeps its own fixed pair: the inferred tier is the weaker
# claim and always takes the muted colour.
TIER_COLORS = {"Direct": RISK, "Inferred": MIXED}


def barh(series, title, xlabel, color=ACCENT, fmt_pct=False, figsize=(7.2, 4.4)):
    s = series.sort_values(ascending=True)
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=figsize)
    ax.barh(s.index, s.values, color=color)
    total = s.sum()
    for y, v in enumerate(s.values):
        lbl = f"{v:,} ({v / total * 100:.0f}%)" if fmt_pct else f"{v:,}"
        ax.text(v, y, " " + lbl, va="center", ha="left", fontsize=8, color=INK)
    ax.set_xlabel(xlabel)
    ax.set_title(title)
    ax.margins(x=0.16)
    ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()


def basemap(ax):
    """CartoDB Positron behind an EPSG:4326 scatter; silent no-op offline."""
    try:
        import contextily as ctx
        tile_cache = c.ROOT / "data" / "tile_cache"
        tile_cache.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        ctx.set_cache_dir(str(tile_cache))
        ctx.add_basemap(ax, crs="EPSG:4326", source=ctx.providers.CartoDB.Positron,
                        attribution_size=5)
        ax.grid(visible=False)
    except Exception:
        ax.grid(alpha=0.2)
```

```{python}
eg_on = eg_active[eg_active["activity_class"] == e.ACTIVITY_EN["catering"]]
```

# Introduction

The fourth delivery arrived as two CSVs — `…2026-09-03…табачное изделие.csv`
(`{python} f"{n_tob:,}"` rows) and `…2026-09-04…алкоголь.csv`
(`{python} f"{n_alc:,}"` rows) — with the contractor's assurance that they carry
the same schema as the third delivery.

This report asks three questions in order. **Is it the same schema?** **What is
actually in it?** And **does it hold up against the two benchmarks this project
can check it with** — the 2022 study, and the FSRAR consolidated licence
registry profiled in `reports/egais/eda-egais.pdf`.

The short answer to the first is *as a container, yes; as a vocabulary, no, and
the difference is not cosmetic*. The short answer to the third is that the
delivery does one important thing very well and one thing not at all.

## Why this delivery exists

`reports/egais/eda-egais.pdf` closed on a specific finding: the commissioned
exports **undercount alcohol retail roughly fivefold**. The third delivery
recognised `{python} f"{(v3['category_2022'] == 'Alcohol shops').sum()}"`
`Alcohol shops` city-wide against
`{python} f"{len(eg_off)}"` alcohol retail licences in force, and the gap was
worst in the outlying okrugs — which biased every okrug risk comparison toward
the centre. The structural reason was that chains sell alcohol under a grocery
licence and so never appear as an alcohol shop.

This delivery is the answer to that. Its whole content is a judgement about
which existing objects plausibly sell alcohol or tobacco.

# Part I — Is it the same schema? {#sec-schema}

## The container: identical

```{python}
# | label: tbl-schema
# | tbl-cap: "Column schema against the third delivery. Names, order and inferred dtypes all agree."
same_cols = list(tob.columns[:22]) == list(v3.columns[:22]) == list(alc.columns[:22])
raw_v3 = pd.read_csv(c.V3_CSV, sep=";", encoding="utf-8-sig", low_memory=False)
raw_t = pd.read_csv(v4.V4_TOBACCO, sep=";", encoding="utf-8-sig", low_memory=False)
raw_a = pd.read_csv(v4.V4_ALCOHOL, sep=";", encoding="utf-8-sig", low_memory=False)
dtype_diffs = {k for k in raw_v3.columns
               if not (str(raw_v3[k].dtype) == str(raw_t[k].dtype) == str(raw_a[k].dtype))}

Markdown(pd.DataFrame([
    {"Check": "Column names and order identical to v3",
     "Result": "yes" if (list(raw_t.columns) == list(raw_v3.columns)
                         and list(raw_a.columns) == list(raw_v3.columns)) else "no"},
    {"Check": "Columns with a differing dtype",
     "Result": f"{len(dtype_diffs)}"},
    {"Check": "Delimiter / encoding", "Result": "semicolon, UTF-8 with BOM — as v3"},
    {"Check": "Duplicate rows", "Result": f"{raw_t.duplicated().sum() + raw_a.duplicated().sum()}"},
    {"Check": "Rows outside Arkhangelsk (city_orig)",
     "Result": f"{(raw_t['city_orig'] != 'Архангельск').sum() + (raw_a['city_orig'] != 'Архангельск').sum()}"},
]).to_markdown(index=False))
```

Anything in this repository that reads the third delivery reads these files
unchanged. That part of the promise holds, and it is worth saying plainly
because the previous three deliveries each broke it somewhere.

## The vocabulary: a fourth taxonomy

`category_orig` and `type_orig` share **no value** with any earlier delivery.
Each file carries exactly one category, and four types between them.

```{python}
# | label: tbl-vocab
# | tbl-cap: "The fourth vocabulary. The 'возможная' (possible) types are an inference by the contractor, not an observation."
vocab = (both.groupby(["risk", "type_en", "evidence", "trade"], observed=True)
         .size().rename("rows").reset_index()
         .sort_values(["risk", "rows"], ascending=[True, False]))
vocab["trade"] = np.where(vocab["risk"] == "Alcohol", vocab["trade"], "—")
Markdown(vocab.rename(columns={"risk": "Risk", "type_en": "Type (translated)",
                               "evidence": "Tier", "trade": "Trade",
                               "rows": "Rows"}).to_markdown(index=False))
```

## The `возможная` tier is most of the delivery

```{python}
# | label: fig-tier
# | fig-cap: "Evidence tier by risk factor. Four rows in five are an inference from the object's type, which the contractor's own comment says still requires checking."
t = (both.groupby(["risk", "evidence"], observed=True).size().unstack(fill_value=0)
     [v4.EVIDENCE_ORDER])
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 3.2))
left = np.zeros(len(t))
for col in v4.EVIDENCE_ORDER:
    ax.barh(t.index, t[col], left=left, color=TIER_COLORS[col], label=col)
    for y, (v, l) in enumerate(zip(t[col], left)):
        if v:
            ax.text(l + v / 2, y, f"{v:,}\n({v / t.loc[t.index[y]].sum() * 100:.0f}%)",
                    ha="center", va="center", fontsize=8,
                    color="white" if col == "Direct" else "white")
    left = left + t[col].to_numpy()
ax.set_xlabel("Records")
ax.set_title("Direct evidence against inference")
ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
ax.legend(loc="lower right", fontsize=8, framealpha=0.9)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

inf_share = both["evidence"].eq("Inferred").mean()
```

`{python} f"{inf_share * 100:.0f}"` % of the delivery is the inferred tier. The
contractor's `verification_comment` states the limit itself:

> тип объекта подходит, но наличие … продукции **требует отдельной проверки**

These rows say "this is a grocery shop, and grocery shops sell beer and
cigarettes". That is a reasonable inference — @sec-egais shows it is broadly the
*right* one — but it is not an observation, and a headline count that merges the
two tiers is not defensible. Every count below is reported split.

## `recode_2022()` silently drops 93 % of the tobacco file

```{python}
# | label: tbl-recode
# | tbl-cap: "The shared 2022 recoder against the fourth vocabulary. The tobacco rule tests for the stem 'табак'; every label in this delivery spells it 'табач-'."
old_t = c.recode_2022(raw_t).value_counts()
old_a = c.recode_2022(raw_a).value_counts()
new_t = tob["category_2022"].value_counts()
new_a = alc["category_2022"].value_counts()
cmp = pd.DataFrame({
    "v3_common.recode_2022 — tobacco": old_t,
    "v4_common.recode_2022_v4 — tobacco": new_t,
    "v3_common.recode_2022 — alcohol": old_a,
    "v4_common.recode_2022_v4 — alcohol": new_a,
}).fillna(0).astype(int)
display(Markdown(cmp.to_markdown()))

lost = int(old_t.get("Other (outside 2022 scheme)", 0))
```

`v3_common.recode_2022()` tests the category/type/name blob for the substring
**`табак`**. Every label the fourth delivery uses spells the stem **`табач-`**
(`Табачная и никотинсодержащая продукция`, `Возможная продажа табачной
продукции`), which does not contain `табак`. The tobacco rule therefore never
fires, and **`{python} f"{lost}"` of `{python} f"{n_tob}"` rows fall into
`Other`** — only the rows saying `вейп` or `кальян` survive by another route.

This is the same class of defect as the `GROCERY_TYPES` case mismatch already
on record, and it fails the same way: silently, with a plausible-looking
distribution. The alcohol file is unaffected, because `алкогол` does match its
labels.

The fix is one stem, and it lives in `v4_common.recode_2022_v4()` — kept out of
`v3_common` on purpose, so the three already-rendered v3 reports keep producing
the numbers they were signed off on.

## Provider mix diverges sharply between the two files

```{python}
# | label: fig-providers
# | fig-cap: "Verification status. The tobacco layer is the best-corroborated file the project has received; the alcohol layer is worse than the third delivery it is drawn from."
mix = pd.DataFrame({
    "v3 export": v3["verification_status"].value_counts(normalize=True),
    "v4 tobacco": tob["verification_status"].value_counts(normalize=True),
    "v4 alcohol": alc["verification_status"].value_counts(normalize=True),
}).fillna(0).mul(100)
order = ["confirmed_by_2gis_and_osm", "only_2gis", "only_osm"]
mix = mix.reindex(order)
labels = [c.STATUS_EN.get(i, i) for i in mix.index]
colors = {"v3 export": OLD, "v4 tobacco": ACCENT, "v4 alcohol": RISK}

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 3.6))
w, x = 0.26, np.arange(len(mix))
for k, col in enumerate(mix.columns):
    ax.bar(x + (k - 1) * w, mix[col], w, color=colors[col], label=col)
    for xi, v in zip(x + (k - 1) * w, mix[col]):
        ax.text(xi, v, f"{v:.0f}%", ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=7, color=INK)
ax.set_xticks(x, labels, fontsize=9)
ax.set_ylabel("% of records")
ax.set_title("Which providers found the object")
ax.grid(axis="x", visible=False)
ax.legend(fontsize=8, framealpha=0.9)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

osm_only_alc = alc["verification_status"].eq("only_osm").mean()
both_alc = int(alc["verification_status"].eq("confirmed_by_2gis_and_osm").sum())
```

The two layers were evidently built by different routes. The tobacco file draws
**`{python} f"{tob['verification_status'].eq('only_2gis').mean() * 100:.0f}"` %**
of its records from 2GIS and confirms
`{python} f"{tob['verification_status'].eq('confirmed_by_2gis_and_osm').mean() * 100:.0f}"` %
with both providers — three times the third delivery's corroboration rate.

The alcohol file is the opposite:
**`{python} f"{osm_only_alc * 100:.1f}"` % rests on OSM alone**, and only
`{python} f"{both_alc}"` records are confirmed by both. That is *worse* than the
third delivery. Whatever the alcohol layer's merits — and @sec-egais finds them
substantial — its own `verification_status` column does not support calling it
verified.

## Field completeness

```{python}
# | label: fig-completeness
# | fig-cap: "Field completeness. Two columns carried over from the third delivery remain unusable, and the match columns are now more missing than before."
cols = [x for x in raw_v3.columns]
comp = pd.DataFrame({
    "v3 export": raw_v3[cols].notna().mean(),
    "v4 tobacco": raw_t[cols].notna().mean(),
    "v4 alcohol": raw_a[cols].notna().mean(),
}).mul(100)
comp = comp.loc[comp.min(axis=1) < 99.5].sort_values("v4 alcohol")

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 4.6))
w, y = 0.26, np.arange(len(comp))
for k, col in enumerate(comp.columns):
    ax.barh(y + (k - 1) * w, comp[col], w, color=colors[col], label=col)
ax.set_yticks(y, comp.index, fontsize=8)
ax.set_xlabel("% populated")
ax.set_xlim(0, 108)
ax.set_title("Columns that are not fully populated")
ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
ax.legend(fontsize=8, loc="lower right", framealpha=0.9)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

Three things to carry forward:

- **`website_check_status` is empty for all `{python} f"{n_tob + n_alc:,}"`
  rows**, exactly as in the third delivery. The column has never held a value in
  any delivery.
- **`opening_date_orig`** is populated for
  `{python} f"{(raw_t['opening_date_orig'].notna().sum() + raw_a['opening_date_orig'].notna().sum())}"`
  rows. Opening-date analysis remains impossible.
- **`match_distance_meters` / `match_name_similarity` got worse.** They are null
  for `{python} f"{raw_t['match_distance_meters'].isna().mean() * 100:.1f}"` %
  of tobacco and
  `{python} f"{raw_a['match_distance_meters'].isna().mean() * 100:.1f}"` % of
  alcohol rows, against
  `{python} f"{raw_v3['match_distance_meters'].isna().mean() * 100:.1f}"` % in
  v3; and where present they still sit at exactly 0 m for
  `{python} f"{(raw_a['match_distance_meters'] == 0).mean() * 100:.0f}"` % of the
  alcohol file. They remain a deduplication key, not independent verification.

## `opening_hours_orig` holds two incompatible encodings

```{python}
# | label: tbl-hours
# | tbl-cap: "Encoding of opening_hours_orig. One column, two formats, split by which provider supplied the row."
hrs = pd.concat([
    v4.hours_frame(tob).assign(layer="v4 tobacco"),
    v4.hours_frame(alc).assign(layer="v4 alcohol"),
])
tab = (hrs.groupby(["layer", "hours_encoding"]).size().unstack(fill_value=0)
       .rename(columns={"json": "2GIS JSON object", "osm": "OSM opening_hours string",
                        "none": "empty"})
       .rename_axis("Layer"))
Markdown(tab.to_markdown())
```

2GIS-sourced rows carry a JSON object keyed by weekday; OSM-sourced rows carry
an OSM `opening_hours` string such as `Mo-Su 08:00-22:00`. A reader that assumes
either format silently loses the other half. The trap exists in the third
delivery too — it is simply more visible here, because the tobacco layer's 2GIS
share is so much higher. `v4_common.parse_hours()` handles both and reports
which it found.

# Part III — Provenance: this re-tags the third delivery {#sec-provenance}

The files are named like exports and dated four days apart, which invites
reading them as new fieldwork. They are not.

```{python}
# | label: tbl-provenance
# | tbl-cap: "Distance from each fourth-delivery record to the nearest object already in the third delivery."
rows = []
for lbl, d in [("v4 tobacco", tob), ("v4 alcohol", alc)]:
    nn = v4.nearest_v3(d, v3)["v3_distance_m"]
    hit, tot = v4.source_id_overlap(d, v3)
    rows.append({
        "Layer": lbl,
        "Records": len(d),
        "Same coordinate": f"{(nn <= 0.5).mean() * 100:.1f} %",
        "Within 10 m": f"{(nn <= 10).mean() * 100:.1f} %",
        "Within 100 m": f"{(nn <= 100).mean() * 100:.1f} %",
        "Source ids in v3": f"{hit}/{tot} ({hit / tot * 100:.0f} %)",
    })
Markdown(pd.DataFrame(rows).to_markdown(index=False))
```

Every tobacco record and all but two alcohol records sit within 100 m of an
object the third delivery already held, and almost all of their OSM/2GIS source
ids are ids v3 already cites. **The fourth delivery adds no geographic
coverage.** What it adds is a classification.

That is not a criticism — it is precisely what was asked for — but it settles
how the delivery may be described. It cannot be cited as an independent
enumeration of alcohol or tobacco outlets, because it shares its object pool,
its providers and its errors with the export it is drawn from.

## What the third delivery had called these objects

```{python}
# | label: tbl-was
# | tbl-cap: "The 2022 class of the nearest third-delivery object, within 50 m. The delivery's substance is the promotion of grocery shops and catering into the risk classes."
out = {}
for lbl, d in [("Tobacco layer", tob), ("Alcohol layer", alc)]:
    nn = v4.nearest_v3(d, v3)
    ok = nn["v3_distance_m"] <= 50
    out[lbl] = nn.loc[ok, "v3_category_2022"].value_counts()
was = pd.DataFrame(out).fillna(0).astype(int)
was = was.reindex([k for k in c.CLASS_ORDER if k in was.index]).rename_axis("v3 class")
display(Markdown(was.to_markdown()))

med_fp = int(was.loc["Medical"].sum()) if "Medical" in was.index else 0
```

This is the delivery's whole content in one table. The third delivery's
`Grocery shops` and `Catering` classes are where the new risk objects come
from — which is exactly the mechanism `reports/egais/eda-egais.pdf` named for
the fivefold undercount: chains sell alcohol under a grocery licence, and cafés
serve it without being bars.

One caveat falls out of the same table. `{python} f"{med_fp}"` records match a
**medical** object — pharmacies caught by the type rule. They are false
positives for both risk factors and should be dropped before any risk index is
built.

# Part IV — Against the 2022 benchmark {#sec-2022}

The 2022 study enumerated `{python} f"{(ref['category_2022'] == 'Alcohol shops').sum()}"`
alcohol shops and `{python} f"{(ref['category_2022'] == 'Tobacco outlets').sum()}"`
tobacco outlets across three okrugs. The matcher is the one used in
`reports/v3/eda-v3-validation.pdf` — 50 m block, rapidfuzz `WRatio` ≥ 0.90 for
an exact tier, ≥ 0.75 for probable — run here without modification.

```{python}
# | label: tbl-recall
# | tbl-cap: "Recall of the 2022 risk objects, in the three okrugs the 2022 study covers. The fourth delivery does not improve on the third."
O3 = c.OKRUGS_2022
r3 = ref[ref["okrug_key"].isin(O3)]
a3 = alc[alc["okrug_key"].isin(O3)]
t3 = tob[tob["okrug_key"].isin(O3)]

rows = []
for eclass, targets in [
    ("Alcohol shops", [("v3 export (all objects)", v3),
                       ("v3 Alcohol shops only", v3[v3["category_2022"] == "Alcohol shops"]),
                       ("v4 alcohol layer", alc),
                       ("v4 alcohol, direct tier", alc[alc["evidence"] == "Direct"])]),
    ("Tobacco outlets", [("v3 export (all objects)", v3),
                         ("v3 Tobacco outlets only", v3[v3["category_2022"] == "Tobacco outlets"]),
                         ("v4 tobacco layer", tob),
                         ("v4 tobacco, direct tier", tob[tob["evidence"] == "Direct"])]),
]:
    etalon = r3[r3["category_2022"] == eclass]
    for lbl, tgt in targets:
        r = m.recall(m.match(etalon, tgt))
        rows.append({"2022 class": eclass, "n": r["n"], "Matched against": lbl,
                     "Exact": r["exact"], "Probable": r["probable"],
                     "Same site, other name": r["gps_only"],
                     "No object <50 m": r["unmatched"],
                     "Recall": f"{r['recall_pct']:.1f} %"})
rec = pd.DataFrame(rows)
display(Markdown(rec.to_markdown(index=False)))

_al = rec[rec["2022 class"] == "Alcohol shops"]
_tb = rec[rec["2022 class"] == "Tobacco outlets"]
r_v3_al = _al.iloc[0]["Recall"]; r_v4_al = _al.iloc[2]["Recall"]
r_v3_tb = _tb.iloc[0]["Recall"]; r_v4_tb = _tb.iloc[2]["Recall"]
```

Recall of the 2022 alcohol shops moves from `{python} r_v3_al` to
`{python} r_v4_al`, and tobacco from `{python} r_v3_tb` to `{python} r_v4_tb`.
**Against the 2022 list the fourth delivery is not an improvement.**

That is less damning than it looks, and the `Same site, other name` column says
why. Counting objects matched at *any* tier, including a same-site match under a
different name:

```{python}
# | label: fig-site
# | fig-cap: "2022 risk objects with some fourth-delivery object at the same site, split by whether the name also agrees. Most of the shortfall is a rebrand, not an absence."
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 3.2))
labels, named, sited = [], [], []
for eclass, tgt in [("Alcohol shops", alc), ("Tobacco outlets", tob)]:
    etalon = r3[r3["category_2022"] == eclass]
    r = m.recall(m.match(etalon, tgt))
    labels.append(f"2022 {eclass}\n(n={r['n']})")
    named.append(100 * (r["exact"] + r["probable"]) / r["n"])
    sited.append(100 * r["gps_only"] / r["n"])
y = np.arange(len(labels))
ax.barh(y, named, color=RISK, label="Name agrees")
ax.barh(y, sited, left=named, color=MIXED, label="Same site, different name")
for yi, (a_, b_) in enumerate(zip(named, sited)):
    ax.text(a_ / 2, yi, f"{a_:.0f}%", ha="center", va="center", color="white", fontsize=9)
    ax.text(a_ + b_ / 2, yi, f"{b_:.0f}%", ha="center", va="center", color="white", fontsize=9)
    ax.text(a_ + b_, yi, f"  {a_ + b_:.0f}% total", va="center", fontsize=8, color=INK)
ax.set_yticks(y, labels, fontsize=9)
ax.set_xlabel("% of the 2022 objects")
ax.set_xlim(0, 108)
ax.set_title("Coverage of the 2022 risk objects by the fourth delivery")
ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
ax.legend(fontsize=8, loc="lower right", framealpha=0.9)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

Four years is long enough for a small alcohol shop to change hands and its sign;
a same-site match under a different name is usually continuity, not error. But
this cannot be *shown* from the data, only argued, so the honest statement is
that the fourth delivery neither improves nor degrades agreement with 2022.

```{python}
# | label: tbl-new
# | tbl-cap: "The other direction: how much of the fourth delivery in the three 2022 okrugs is new relative to the 2022 list."
rows = []
for lbl, tgt, eclass in [("v4 alcohol", a3, "Alcohol shops"),
                         ("v4 tobacco", t3, "Tobacco outlets")]:
    etalon = r3[r3["category_2022"] == eclass]
    lab = m.reverse_coverage(tgt, m.match(etalon, tgt))
    rows.append({"Layer": lbl, "Rows (3 okrugs)": len(tgt),
                 "Match a 2022 object": int((lab == "Reproduced from 2022").sum()),
                 "New": int((lab == "New in v3").sum()),
                 "% new": f"{(lab == 'New in v3').mean() * 100:.1f} %"})
Markdown(pd.DataFrame(rows).to_markdown(index=False))
```

The overwhelming majority of the layer has no 2022 counterpart — because it is
mostly the inferred tier, and the 2022 study never tried to enumerate ordinary
shops that happen to sell beer. The 2022 list is therefore the **wrong
benchmark** for this delivery. The right one is the licence registry.

# Part V — Against the FSRAR licence registry {#sec-egais}

The licence registry is the only genuinely independent check available: a state
register, compiled for a different purpose, sharing neither providers nor
method with the contractor. Its limits are those established in
`reports/egais/eda-egais.pdf` — it holds **alcohol only**, so the tobacco layer
is untestable here, and it is a *register*, so only rows in force count.

Restricted to mainland city rows in force, it holds
**`{python} f"{len(eg_off)}"` off-trade** and
**`{python} f"{len(eg_on)}"` on-trade** retail licences.

## The fivefold gap closes

```{python}
# | label: fig-headline
# | fig-cap: "Alcohol availability city-wide, counted four ways. The third delivery's Alcohol shops class sat far below the licence count; the fourth delivery's off-trade layer sits slightly above it."
_key = (eg_off["outlet_street"].map(e.norm_street) + "|"
        + eg_off["outlet_house"].astype(str).str.lower().str.strip())
n_eg_outlets = int(_key.nunique())

head = pd.Series({
    "v3 export\n'Alcohol shops'": int((v3["category_2022"] == "Alcohol shops").sum()),
    "Licence registry\ndistinct outlets": n_eg_outlets,
    "Licence registry\nlicences in force": len(eg_off),
    "v4 alcohol\noff-trade": len(alc_off),
})
cols_ = [OLD, GREEN, GREEN, RISK]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 3.8))
ax.bar(head.index, head.values, color=cols_)
for xi, v in enumerate(head.values):
    ax.text(xi, v, f"{v:,}", ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=10, color=INK)
ax.set_ylabel("Outlets selling alcohol for off-premises consumption")
ax.set_title("Off-trade alcohol availability, four counts")
ax.set_xticks(range(len(head)), head.index, fontsize=8)
ax.grid(axis="x", visible=False)
ax.margins(y=0.16)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

ratio_v3 = len(eg_off) / max((v3["category_2022"] == "Alcohol shops").sum(), 1)
ratio_v4 = len(eg_off) / len(alc_off)
```

The third delivery recognised one alcohol shop for every
**`{python} f"{ratio_v3:.1f}"`** licences in force. The fourth delivery's
off-trade layer sits at **`{python} f"{ratio_v4:.2f}"`** — it now names slightly
*more* outlets than there are licences, which is the expected direction: the
inferred tier will include shops that sell no alcohol, and one licence can cover
a chain outlet that the register lists once.

On-trade agrees less well — `{python} f"{len(alc_on)}"` objects against
`{python} f"{len(eg_on)}"` licences in force — but the on-trade layer is
`{python} f"{alc_on['evidence'].eq('Inferred').mean() * 100:.0f}"` % inferred
from "this is a café", and many cafés genuinely serve no alcohol. Treat the
on-trade count as an upper bound.

## The okrug bias is substantially repaired

This matters more than the city total. The undercount was not uniform: it was
mildest in the centre and worst in the outlying okrugs, which meant any okrug
risk comparison built on the third delivery was biased *toward* the centre.

```{python}
# | label: tbl-okrug-ratio
# | tbl-cap: "Active off-trade licences per export object, by okrug. A ratio far above 1 means the export missed outlets; the third delivery's spread ran from 2.9 to 12.0."
okr = pd.DataFrame({
    "v3 Alcohol shops": v3[v3["category_2022"] == "Alcohol shops"]["okrug_key"].value_counts(),
    "v4 off-trade": alc_off["okrug_key"].value_counts(),
    "Licences in force": eg_off["okrug_key"].value_counts(),
}).reindex(OKRUG_ORDER).fillna(0).astype(int)
okr["Ratio vs v3"] = okr["Licences in force"] / okr["v3 Alcohol shops"].replace(0, np.nan)
okr["Ratio vs v4"] = okr["Licences in force"] / okr["v4 off-trade"].replace(0, np.nan)
_show = okr.copy().rename_axis("Okrug")
_show["Ratio vs v3"] = _show["Ratio vs v3"].map("{:.1f}".format)
_show["Ratio vs v4"] = _show["Ratio vs v4"].map("{:.2f}".format)
display(Markdown(_show.to_markdown(disable_numparse=True)))

sp3 = okr["Ratio vs v3"].max() / okr["Ratio vs v3"].min()
sp4 = okr["Ratio vs v4"].max() / okr["Ratio vs v4"].min()
```

```{python}
# | label: fig-okrug-ratio
# | fig-cap: "The same ratios, plotted. A perfectly calibrated export would sit on the dashed line at 1.0. The third delivery's error grows with distance from the centre; the fourth delivery's does not."
o = okr.sort_values("Licences in force", ascending=True)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 4.4))
y = np.arange(len(o))
ax.scatter(o["Ratio vs v3"], y, s=64, color=OLD, edgecolor="white",
           zorder=3, label="Licences per v3 'Alcohol shop'")
ax.scatter(o["Ratio vs v4"], y, s=64, color=RISK, edgecolor="white",
           zorder=3, label="Licences per v4 off-trade object")
for yi in y:
    ax.plot([o["Ratio vs v4"].iloc[yi], o["Ratio vs v3"].iloc[yi]], [yi, yi],
            color=MIXED, lw=1, alpha=0.5, zorder=2)
ax.axvline(1.0, color=INK, ls="--", lw=1, zorder=1)
ax.text(1.0, -0.75, " parity", fontsize=8, color=INK, va="center")
ax.set_yticks(y, o.index, fontsize=9)
ax.set_ylim(-1.1, len(o) - 0.3)
ax.set_xscale("log")
ax.set_xticks([0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10], ["0.5", "1", "2", "5", "10"])
ax.set_xlabel("Active off-trade licences per export object (log scale)")
ax.set_title("Calibration against the licence registry, by okrug")
ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
ax.legend(fontsize=8, loc="lower right", framealpha=0.9)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

The third delivery's ratios spread over a factor of
**`{python} f"{sp3:.1f}"`** across okrugs — 12 licences per recognised shop in
Tsiglomensky against 2.9 in Lomonosovsky. The fourth delivery's spread is a
factor of **`{python} f"{sp4:.1f}"`**, and every okrug sits between
`{python} f"{okr['Ratio vs v4'].min():.2f}"` and
`{python} f"{okr['Ratio vs v4'].max():.2f}"`. **Okrug-level alcohol risk
comparisons become defensible for the first time in this project.**

## Spatial corroboration, both directions

Counts can agree while pointing at different places. This checks the locations.

```{python}
# | label: tbl-corrob
# | tbl-cap: "Two-way spatial agreement between the alcohol layer and licensed outlets in force. The reverse direction — licensed outlets the export can see — is the one the fivefold-undercount finding was about."
corr_v4 = v4.corroboration(alc_off, eg_off)
corr_v3 = v4.corroboration(v3[v3["category_2022"] == "Alcohol shops"], eg_off)
tabc = pd.DataFrame({
    "Radius": [f"{r} m" for r in corr_v4["radius_m"]],
    "v3 shop near licence": [f"{x} %" for x in corr_v3["v4_near_licence_pct"]],
    "Licence near v3 shop": [f"{x} %" for x in corr_v3["licence_near_v4_pct"]],
    "v4 object near licence": [f"{x} %" for x in corr_v4["v4_near_licence_pct"]],
    "Licence near v4 object": [f"{x} %" for x in corr_v4["licence_near_v4_pct"]],
})
display(Markdown(tabc.to_markdown(index=False)))

rev3_50 = corr_v3.set_index("radius_m").loc[50, "licence_near_v4_pct"]
rev4_50 = corr_v4.set_index("radius_m").loc[50, "licence_near_v4_pct"]
rev4_100 = corr_v4.set_index("radius_m").loc[100, "licence_near_v4_pct"]
```

Read the fourth column. The share of licensed outlets in force with a matching
export object within 50 m rises from **`{python} f"{rev3_50}"` %** under the
third delivery to **`{python} f"{rev4_50}"` %** under the fourth, and reaches
`{python} f"{rev4_100}"` % at 100 m. The remaining gap is consistent with the
registry's own coordinate quality, which
`reports/egais/eda-egais.pdf` shows is missing for a substantial minority of
rows and biased toward recently issued licences.

```{python}
# | label: fig-map
# | fig-cap: "Licensed off-trade outlets in force (green) against the fourth delivery's off-trade objects (orange), on an OpenStreetMap/CARTO basemap. The two surfaces now cover the same city."
pts_eg = eg_off.dropna(subset=["latitude", "longitude"])
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 6.6))
ax.scatter(alc_off["longitude"], alc_off["latitude"], s=14, alpha=0.65,

           label=f"v4 off-trade object ({len(alc_off):,})")
ax.scatter(pts_eg["longitude"], pts_eg["latitude"], s=26, alpha=0.85,
           color=GREEN, edgecolor="white", linewidth=0.4, marker="^",
           label=f"Licence in force ({len(pts_eg):,})")
ax.set_xlabel("Longitude")
ax.set_ylabel("Latitude")
ax.set_title("The alcohol layer against the licence registry")
```

# Part VI — The risk surface {#sec-surface}

With the calibration established, the layer can be read as a risk surface.

```{python}
# | label: fig-okrug-density
# | fig-cap: "Risk sites per 100 objects in the third delivery's pool, by okrug. The outlying okrugs carry a markedly higher share of risk objects than the centre."
dens = pd.DataFrame({
    "risk_sites": sites["okrug_key"].value_counts(),
    "all_objects": v3["okrug_key"].value_counts(),
}).reindex(OKRUG_ORDER).fillna(0)
dens["per_100"] = 100 * dens["risk_sites"] / dens["all_objects"]
d = dens.sort_values("per_100")

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 4.4))
ax.barh(d.index, d["per_100"], color=RISK)
for yi, (v, n_) in enumerate(zip(d["per_100"], d["risk_sites"])):
    ax.text(v, yi, f"  {v:.1f}  (n={int(n_)})", va="center", fontsize=8, color=INK)
ax.set_xlabel("Risk sites per 100 objects in the v3 pool")
ax.set_title("Concentration of alcohol/tobacco sites, by okrug")
ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
ax.margins(x=0.20)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

The gradient runs from the two central okrugs at roughly
`{python} f"{dens.loc['Lomonosovsky', 'per_100']:.0f}"` risk sites per 100
objects to Tsiglomensky at
`{python} f"{dens.loc['Tsiglomensky', 'per_100']:.0f}"`. Read this as
*composition*, not absolute density: the outlying okrugs have fewer objects of
every kind, and a larger share of what they do have is a shop that sells beer
and cigarettes. A per-capita reading would need population by okrug, which no
delivery has supplied.

```{python}
# | label: fig-map-risk
# | fig-cap: "The combined risk layer. Sites carrying both an alcohol and a tobacco row are drawn last, in purple."
s_al = sites[(sites["risk"] == "Alcohol") & ~sites["dual"]]
s_tb = sites[(sites["risk"] == "Tobacco") & ~sites["dual"]]
s_du = sites[sites["dual"]]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 6.6))
for sub, col, lbl in [(s_al, RISK, "Alcohol only"), (s_tb, ACCENT, "Tobacco only"),
                      (s_du, PURPLE, "Both")]:
    ax.scatter(sub["longitude"], sub["latitude"], s=14, alpha=0.75,
               color=col, edgecolor="white", linewidth=0.25,
               label=f"{lbl} ({len(sub):,})")
ax.set_xlabel("Longitude")
ax.set_ylabel("Latitude")
ax.set_title("Alcohol and tobacco risk sites")
ax.set_aspect(1 / np.cos(np.deg2rad(64.54)))
basemap(ax)
ax.legend(loc="upper left", fontsize=8, markerscale=1.4, framealpha=0.9)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## The tobacco layer has no benchmark

Everything in @sec-egais applies to alcohol only. The licence registry holds
**no tobacco class at all** — the regulator's remit covers both, the published
data does not — and the 2022 tobacco list is
`{python} f"{(ref['category_2022'] == 'Tobacco outlets').sum()}"` objects in
three okrugs, which @sec-2022 shows the delivery reproduces about a third of by
name.

So the `{python} f"{n_tob}"`-object tobacco layer rests on the contractor's
inference and on 2GIS category labels, and **nothing in this repository can
check it**. Its high 2GIS corroboration rate is a point in its favour and is not
the same thing as verification. Report tobacco results with that stated.

# Conclusions

**On the schema question.** The contractor's promise holds where it is easy to
check and fails where it is not. The 22 columns, their order and their types are
identical to the third delivery, so existing code reads the files unchanged. But
`category_orig` and `type_orig` carry a fourth vocabulary sharing no value with
any earlier delivery, and the project's shared `recode_2022()` silently drops
`{python} f"{lost}"` of `{python} f"{n_tob}"` tobacco rows on it. Schema
compatibility at the column level is not schema compatibility.

**On what the delivery is.** It is a risk-attribution layer over the third
delivery, not a fourth survey: every tobacco record and all but two alcohol
records sit within 100 m of an object v3 already held. Four rows in five are an
inference from the object's type, which the contractor's own comment says
requires separate checking. It should be described as a classification of
existing objects, and its two tiers reported separately.

**On the 2022 benchmark.** No improvement — recall moves from
`{python} r_v3_al` to `{python} r_v4_al` for alcohol and from
`{python} r_v3_tb` to `{python} r_v4_tb` for tobacco. Most of the shortfall is
same-site rebranding rather than absence, but that is an argument, not a
measurement. The 2022 list is the wrong benchmark for a layer that is mostly
inferred availability.

**On the licence registry — the finding that matters.** The fivefold alcohol
undercount closes. Off-trade objects rise from
`{python} f"{(v3['category_2022'] == 'Alcohol shops').sum()}"` to
`{python} f"{len(alc_off)}"` against `{python} f"{len(eg_off)}"` licences in
force; the licences-per-object ratio moves from
`{python} f"{ratio_v3:.1f}"` to `{python} f"{ratio_v4:.2f}"`; the okrug spread
narrows from a factor of `{python} f"{sp3:.1f}"` to
`{python} f"{sp4:.1f}"`; and the share of licensed outlets visible to the export
within 50 m rises from `{python} f"{rev3_50}"` % to `{python} f"{rev4_50}"` %.
The centre-bias that made okrug comparisons unusable is substantially repaired.

**What still cannot be done.** The tobacco layer has no independent benchmark of
any kind. The alcohol layer is
`{python} f"{osm_only_alc * 100:.1f}"` % OSM-only, so it is well *calibrated*
without being *verified*. `{python} f"{med_fp}"` pharmacies are false positives
and must be removed before any index is built. And the five okrugs outside the
2022 study remain unvalidated against any object-level benchmark — the licence
registry now covers them for alcohol, which is a real gain, but for tobacco
they remain dark.
